editorText:
The door to the mess slid open with a soft hiss, retracting into the hull. The tension in the room thickened. Then, as if on cue, confusion followed awe when a tall, unfamiliar figure stepped through the threshold. The figure’s strange, organic appearance defied everything they had expected. It stood still, its shoulders angled toward John as though it recognised him intimately. But it was unlike anything created by man—a being that seemed to have evolved from something beyond human science.

With a grace that belied its alien form, it bowed its head toward John, the gesture carrying an eerie sense of recognition—like an echo from a distant past.

John rose from his chair to address the figure, but the sudden shift in the ship’s thrust gravity—caused by the uncoupling of the Doctor’s transport pod—sent his balance faltering. His attempt to stand with respect felt disjointed, as scattered as his thoughts had been at the figure’s arrival.

"Looks like he’s planning to stay for a while," Kitten murmured softly to John, her voice almost lost in the subtle hum of the ship.

Through the port window, the Doctor’s pod could be seen drifting back toward the planet’s surface. The atmosphere seemed to wrap around it, pulling it deeper into a blue silhouette until it was swallowed entirely by the distant horizon. The room was awkwardly quiet, as John waited for their new acquaintance to address the room. Yet the voice that spoke up was not that of a male but of a female.

  Nova, It’s me, Doc,”  Said the alien as it looked over in John’s direction once more. “My Son..” The words eased out gently but heavy with history from the being vocal glands. It didn’t have a mouth as such but emitted sound-like vibrations, just as though spoken from a tongue.

Tex’s eyes darted around the room. First to Shai, then Tau then back to John resting once more on the strange alien standing before them. “Well, I’m sorry” Tex proclaimed sarcastically, “ Am I the only one failing to see the fucking resemblance here. Am I missing something?”

“I apologise for the Doctor’s impromptu arrival in his..derived form”. The sentient’s voice eased the lying tension commanding the room as she stood gently beside the Doctor. Tex shied away from the sound of this new sentient’s voice but found it strangely comforting. It was something in the machine’s voice. She or it’s voice, Tex corrected himself to maintain some order with his internal conflict of the rapidly evolving world before him, had reminded him of his long passed sister, who had been lost in the 3rd war.

The strange figure before them looked nothing like the Sentient’s anatomy on the surface, its shape a distant echo perhaps. But this was something more, sophisticated, organic. Shockingly unfamiliar, and so, grotesque, it threw the entire room into shock. “Don’t let my appearance startle you, My primitive sentient body is undergoing some.. Alterations for our next mission, as surprisingly versatile and resilient it is to extreme conditions as our Engineers intended them, I expect we may encounter some, Extraordinary circumstances on Oasis, and so preparations were in order.” John’s face was riddled still with confusion, trying to find sense in what was happening averting his gaze from the constant directed eyes upon him.

“What have you got us into” they said, he could hear their thoughts, but he persisted, fixing his eyes on the mess table, his chin resting as he perched his arm in his elbows cradle “You’re.. A figure of your imagination” John knew what he said made no sense, “You, re-invented your biology to capitalise on the atmospheric make-up of Oasis”. He had never seen the alien standing before them, yet he recognised the speech patterns, it was his father. But he couldn’t piece the alien before him with his father’s youthful face as he remembered it. Is this what his father had become?

"I am simply an evolved version of my prior model," it continued, voice steady. "We had to make adjustments to better adapt to Oasis's ever-changing environment."

As the Doctor spoke, faint blue and green hues danced along its temples, pulsing with emotion—an attempt, it seemed, to mimic sentience, though it was clearly more advanced. Its movements were fluid, more organic than the previous sentient designs.

The creature's outer shell gleamed faintly under the lights, resembling a crustacean that had evolved into a humanoid form. Ports replaced where lungs might have been, housing what appeared to be fuel cells. Its skin had a matte sheen, hard and protective, guarding what lay beneath. Its chest didn’t rise or fall like a human’s but instead emitted a soft hum as it moved through the room.
